display.title: Havdalah: Saying Goodbye to Shabbos and the Havdalah Kit
display.summary_short: What Havdalah means, when we say it after Shabbos, and what goes into a Havdalah kit: wine, a cup, spices and a candle with many wicks.
display.summary_long: A mitzvah-time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. After learning how we welcome Shabbos by lighting candles, Uncle Yossi teaches how we bid Shabbos farewell with Havdalah. The word Havdalah means separation: it separates the holy day of Shabbos from the ordinary weekdays. Just as candles are lit no later than 18 minutes before sunset, Havdalah is said the next night after the stars appear, and because the times change from week to week, it is best to check a Jewish calendar. Before explaining the reasons for Havdalah, he introduces the Havdalah kit: a bottle of wine and a cup, as for Kiddush; a box of fragrant spices, besamim; and a Havdalah candle, which unlike a Shabbos candle must have at least two wicks.
display.lesson: We end Shabbos with Havdalah, separating the holy day from the weekdays, once the stars are out.
